issue.title: rsky-relay: listHosts/getHostStatus return JSON as Content-Type: text/plain
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

`com.atproto.sync.listHosts` and `com.atproto.sync.getHostStatus` return valid JSON with `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`. Both lexicons declare `"encoding": "application/json"` for output. `/_health` is correct (`application/json`).


The cause is [`write_response` in `rsky-relay/src/server/server.rs`](https://github.com/blacksky-algorithms/rsky/blob/aec5598939fa3df724c313b101935c8210536ece/rsky-relay/src/server/server.rs#L202-L208
), which hardcodes `text/plain; charset=utf-8`.


The listHosts and getHostStatus arms pass it `serde_json::to_string(...)` output. On `fix/relay-throughput-parity`, commit 035324e4 added `write_json`, but [only the `/_health` arm uses it](https://github.com/blacksky-algorithms/rsky/blob/aec5598939fa3df724c313b101935c8210536ece/rsky-relay/src/server/server.rs#L400-L432
).

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. `curl -sI "https://atproto.africa/xrpc/com.atproto.sync.listHosts?limit=1" | grep -i content-type`
  1. Output: `content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`
1. `getHostStatus` gives the same result for both 200 and 400 responses, e.g. `curl -sI "https://atproto.africa/xrpc/com.atproto.sync.getHostStatus?hostname=bsky.network"`
  1. Output: `content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8` 

Compare both to `curl -sI https://atproto.africa/_health`, which returns `content-type: application/json`

**Expected behavior**

Responses with JSON bodies should use `Content-Type: application/json`, as the lexicons declare.

**Details**

- Operating system: N/A
- Node version: N/A

Encountered this while building an app that monitors uptime across the ecosystem and had to build an exception. Figured it'd be kind to report the issue.

issue.title: fix(core): resolve thread list load promises once the threads state reports the list
issue.body: ## Problem `aui.threads.getLoadThreadsPromise()` resolves while `aui.threads().getState().isLoading` is still `true`, so code that awaits it and then reads the state sees the list before it loaded. `reload()` and `loadMore()` have the same gap. ## Root cause The promises resolve when the runtime core finishes loading. `aui.threads().getState()` returns the threads client's last committed snapshot, which only catches up after React renders the new core state. ## Change `useAfterStateCommit` delays each load promise until the client has committed a render of the list state that was current when the load settled. A load that settles before the client's first commit waits for it, and a promise resolves at once after the client unmounts. `RemoteThreadList` wraps `getLoadThreadsPromise()`, `reload()` and `loadMore()` with it, and the thread list runtime client does the same. Each underlying promise maps to one delayed promise, so the identities stay as they were: repeated calls during a load share a promise, `reload()` shares it too, and a new load gets a new one. Without this, `use()` warns about an uncached promise and Suspense caches keyed on the promise never settle. The JSDoc in `scopes/threads.ts` now says how the promises settle on failure: `getLoadThreadsPromise()` and `reload()` resolve with `loadError` in state, and `loadMore()` resolves after a failed page request, which it logs. If the client hasn't committed within 100ms of the load settling, the promise resolves anyway. That happens inside the `act()` callback that completes the load, because React holds the commit until `act` returns, and when a Suspense boundary hides the client while a `use()` reader inside it waits on `reload()`. In those cases `getState()` may not report the list yet. The JSDoc says this too. ## Verification - New tests in `RemoteThreadList.load-promise.test.tsx` and `useRemoteThreadListRuntime.load-promise.test.tsx` fail without the fix: state after await for each method (including `loadMore()` with the appended page and cleared `isLoadingMore`), promise identity across calls and reloads, Suspense with `use()` (including a `reload()` read inside the boundary that also holds the client), and awaiting inside the `act()` that completes the load. `useAfterStateCommit.test.tsx` covers a promise that settles before the first commit, and one awaited after unmount. - `@assistant-ui/core` tests: 2756 passed. - Existing tests in `RemoteThreadList.test.ts` and `RemoteThreadList.concurrent.test.tsx` drop the `waitFor` retries after awaiting a load and read the state directly. ## Public surface `@assistant-ui/core`: `getLoadThreadsPromise()`, `reload()` and `loadMore()` resolve after the loaded state is committed, or after 100ms if the client can't commit. Patch changeset. No exports changed. Split out of #8689.

issue.body: Stacked on #8689. ## Problem assistant-ui can't run in a VS Code extension webview without custom plumbing. A webview has no HTTP origin, so `fetch("/api/chat")` has nowhere to go; it needs a nonce-based CSP; the kit's shadcn tokens ignore the VS Code theme; links can't navigate; and `localStorage` doesn't reliably persist. ## Change New package `@assistant-ui/vscode`: - `./webview`: `vscodeFetch` tunnels `fetch` over the webview's `postMessage` channel, so HTTP runtimes work by passing `fetch: vscodeFetch`. `createVSCodeModelAdapter` gives `useLocalRuntime` a `ChatModelAdapter` over the same bridge. `installLinkInterceptor` sends link clicks and `window.open` to the host, `createVSCodeStorage` backs `createLocalStorageAdapter` with an extension Memento, and `getCspNonce` reads the page nonce. - `./host`: `serveWebviewRoutes` runs Next-style route handlers (`(req: Request) => Response`) in the extension host and streams responses back, with aborts mapped to `req.signal`. `serveWebviewHost` adds link opening (scheme-checked again on the host) and storage. `renderWebviewHtml` and `createWebviewCsp` build the page with a strict nonce CSP. The host code doesn't import `vscode`; webviews are typed structurally. - `./theme.css` maps the kit's shadcn tokens to `--vscode-*` variables and points Tailwind's `dark` variant at VS Code's dark and high contrast themes, so components follow theme switches without edits. Also: - `templates/vscode` and `assistant-ui create --template vscode`: an extension with a chat view in the secondary sidebar, running the default template's chat route in the extension host. The API key lives in SecretStorage. - `examples/with-vscode`: a test bed extension with scripted replies (no API key), switchable runtimes and CSP modes, a readiness view of probes, and a gallery of 204 kit sections with a screenshot matrix (Dark Modern, Light Modern, Dark High Contrast at editor and 320px). - Workflows: `vscode-test-bed.yaml` runs the probes headless in VS Code 1.140.0 per runtime at phase 1, retrying a failed probe once and reporting it; `vscode-test-bed-screenshots.yaml` uploads the screenshot contact sheet as an artifact; `vscode-test-bed-combined.yaml` runs both against a base with other branches applied. The generic test job skips `with-vscode`. - Docs: `guides/vscode.mdx` and the CLI template table. ## Verification - `@assistant-ui/vscode`: 92 tests (bridge streaming, UTF-8 split across chunks, 404/405/500, abort, coalescing, concurrent requests, AI SDK end to end, model adapter, CSP builder and escaping, theme token coverage against the default template, link interceptor, storage round trip through `createLocalStorageAdapter`). CLI: 492 tests. Docs: 1336. - Template builds and typechecks; `create --template vscode` scaffolds, builds and packages a `.vsix` with the package installed from a tarball. - Test bed in headless VS Code 1.140 at phase 1: bridge round trip, abort, frontend tool approval, theme following, external links, thread persistence, scaffold drift, chat fixtures and the gallery checks (0 CSP violations, 0 errors, 0 overflow in 204 sections) pass under both the AI SDK and local runtimes, except `threads-persist` under the AI SDK runtime, which needs #8604. - The workflows ran in an Ubuntu 24.04 container; `actionlint` is clean. - `pnpm lint`, `sync-templates`, `typecheck`, `api-surface:check`, `distributions:check`, `declarations:check`, `changesets:check` and `generate:api-reference --strict` pass. ## Public surface - New package `@assistant-ui/vscode` (`./host`, `./webview`, `./theme.css`), patch changesets, API surface file added. Trusted publishing for the new npm name has to be set up before its first release. - `assistant-ui` / `create-assistant-ui`: new `vscode` template. Until `@assistant-ui/vscode` is published, `create --template vscode` fails at install; `--skip-install` works. - Docs: new `guides/vscode.mdx`. It describes an unreleased package, so it should go live with the release. - New workflows under `.github/workflows/vscode-test-bed*.yaml`; `code-quality.yaml` excludes `with-vscode` from the generic test job.
